$schema_note: address, size, range, name, display, group for every editable ZEN-Core tone parameter (docs/BRIEF.md §6). Offsets are relative to a tone-block base (tone_common) or a block base computed from meta.block_relative_offsets (all other blocks). See tools/FINDINGS.md 'M2 sub-problem A/B' sections for the full discovery writeup and tools/zencore_addressing.py for the slot-address formula.

sources: Official Roland JUPITER-Xm MIDI Implementation Ver.3.0+ (static.roland.com/assets/media/pdf/JUPITER-Xm_MIDI_imple_eng01_W.pdf) -- same ZEN-Core engine, model 00 00 00 65. Field names, offsets, sizes, and ranges for tone_common/tone_partial/partial_filter_env/partial_amp_env/partial_lfo below are taken from this document.

Locriana/mcpoker + successor mctools_basic (public domain/Unlicense, github.com/Locriana) -- tone-slot base-address table (meta.slot_addressing.track_base), from zen_core_tools.py's ZenCoreTools.get_base_address().

Live hardware validation against a real MC-707, 2026-08-31 -- see tools/FINDINGS.md. Confirms: Tone Common total size (0x36) exact match; Level (+0x15) audible write+round-trip; Pan (+0x16) value match (0x40 seen on two different tones, consistent with documented center-pan default); Tone Coarse Tune (+0x18) write+round-trip match (mcpoker's own cited known-working DT1 example); tone-slot addressing formula validated at 4 independent addresses (2 previously confirmed by on-device name match, 2 new predictions confirmed live by RQ1 read returning valid structured replies).

validation_tiers.device-confirmed: closed-loop confirmed against the device's own front-panel display, both directions: (1) the user set the on-device control to a known value, this address was read back and exactly matched, and (2) a new value was written via SysEx and the user confirmed the on-device display updated to match. The strongest tier -- ties the address directly to the device's own named parameter, not just 'the sound changed'.
validation_tiers.audible-confirmed: written on real hardware, listened, heard the expected change, round-trip re-read matched
validation_tiers.round-trip-confirmed: written on real hardware, round-trip re-read matched, not independently confirmed by listening
validation_tiers.structural: offset/size taken from the official Jupiter-X/Xm doc; not yet individually read or written against the MC-707, but the containing block's total size and at least one sibling field in it have been confirmed live
validation_tiers.unvalidated: taken from the official doc only; no MC-707-specific cross-check at all yet, including block size

encodings.ascii: N raw bytes, each 0x20-0x7F, one ASCII character per byte
encodings.uint7: 1 raw byte, full value 0-127 (bit 7 always 0, per Roland's 7-bit-clean SysEx data bytes)
encodings.nibble2: 2 raw bytes, MSB-first; value = (byte[0]<<4)|byte[1], each byte's upper nibble always 0000
encodings.nibble4: 4 raw bytes, MSB-first; value = (byte[0]<<12)|(byte[1]<<8)|(byte[2]<<4)|byte[3], each byte's upper nibble always 0000

slot_addressing.description: Base address of a tone slot = track_base[track_idx] + tone_alignment * n, using 7-bit-carry (base-128) addition, NOT plain 32-bit hex addition -- see tools/zencore_addressing.py::add_7bit_carry and tools/FINDINGS.md 'M2 sub-problem A solved' for why plain hex addition is wrong for tracks 4 and 8. n = clip_idx (0-15) for a clip tone, or 16 for the track's own 'track sound' tone.

block_relative_offsets._note: tone_partial/partial_pitch_env/partial_filter_env/partial_amp_env/partial_eq index by partial (1-4, i.e. array index 0-3), each block strided 0x000100 apart. partial_lfo is strided 0x000200 apart (double) -- likely because it packs both LFO and Mod LFO; only LFO1's own fields are mapped below (0x00-0x1D), the rest of that block is unmapped. tone_mfx, tone_pmt, synth_common, synth_pmt, synth_partial are declared (address only) but their fields are NOT mapped yet -- explicitly deferred per docs/M2_PLAN.md (MFX especially: 93 effect types, a later pass).

tone_common.validation_note: Total size (0x36) and 3 individual fields (Level, Pan, Tone Coarse Tune) confirmed live -- see tools/FINDINGS.md.

fields.name: Level
fields.note: DT1-wrote 0x00, tone went silent, restored to 0x54, re-confirmed audible. See tools/FINDINGS.md M1 steps 3&4.

fields.name: Pan
fields.note: 0x40 (center) observed on two different tones. IMPORTANT (2026-08-31): confirmed this is NOT the same control as the device's MIXER screen pan -- user set Mixer pan hard left on Track 1, this address still read back 0x40 (center), unchanged. This field is very likely the ZEN-Core patch-internal pan (matches the official doc's offset exactly, same block as the confirmed Level field), but the Mixer's pan is evidently a separate parameter in a different, not-yet-located address space (probably the 0x10000000 'system/track settings' region -- see sys_ex_comm.py's own track-color example at that same base). Not yet closed-loop confirmed against any on-device control. See tools/FINDINGS.md.

fields.name: Tone Coarse Tune
fields.note: mcpoker's own known-working DT1 example (docs/BRIEF.md §3): wrote 0x42, round-trip re-read matched. Not confirmed by listening yet.

fields.name: Portamento Time
fields.note: Earlier single-byte DT1 writes to +0x26 and +0x27 (this field's 3rd/4th nibble bytes) were both silently rejected -- likely because the device only accepts a write at a field's declared START offset (0x24) spanning its full width (4 bytes), not into the middle of a packed multi-byte value. See tools/FINDINGS.md.

fields.name: Bend Range Up
fields.note: Earlier value-sweep test (0/1/3/5/8) produced no confirmed audible change -- consistent with this field not affecting a static held note's timbre.

tone_partial.coverage_note: Only offsets 0x00-0x4F are mapped (block continues further, priority core-mixer/filter fields only -- see docs/M2_PLAN.md scope).

fields.name: Pan
fields.note: Confirmed 2026-08-31 on Track 1's track-sound slot, Partial 1: user set on-device SOUND EDIT > AMP > PAN PLT1 to L64, read back 0x00 (exact match); then wrote 0x40 via SysEx, user confirmed the on-device PLT1 display updated to center. Full bidirectional closed-loop confirmation -- distinct from Tone Common's own Pan (+0x16 in that block), which is NOT the same as this per-partial pan or the Mixer screen's pan (see that field's note). See tools/FINDINGS.md.

fields.name: TVF Filter Type
fields.display: OFF, LPF, BPF, HPF, PKG, LPF2, LPF3

fields.name: TVF Cutoff Frequency
fields.note: Confirmed 2026-08-31 on Track 1's track-sound slot, Partial 1: also audible (wrote 100, was 1023, user heard the change on a held note). Later closed-loop confirmed bidirectionally: user set on-device SOUND EDIT (Easy Mode) Cutoff Frequency to 492, read back decoded to exactly 492; wrote 800 via SysEx, user confirmed the on-device display updated to 800; restored to 492. Easy Mode appears to write the same value to all 4 partials at once. See tools/FINDINGS.md.

fields.name: TVF Resonance
fields.note: Confirmed 2026-08-31 on Track 1's track-sound slot, Partial 1: also audible (wrote 800, was 8, user heard the sustained note become more resonant). Later closed-loop confirmed bidirectionally: user set on-device Resonance to 27, read back decoded to exactly 27; wrote 500 via SysEx, user confirmed the on-device display updated to 500; restored to 27. See tools/FINDINGS.md.

partial_lfo.coverage_note: IMPORTANT (2026-08-31): the device's Easy Mode tone-edit screen shows TWO independent LFO tabs (labelled 'LFO 1' and 'LFO 2' in the UI) for a single partial, with visibly different Waveform/Rate/Depth values on each. This block (relative offset 0x3000, which the official doc's ZCore address-map table calls 'Partial LFO 1') was confirmed to be the data behind the UI's 'LFO 2' tab, not 'LFO 1' -- 6 independent fields (Waveform, Rate, Pitch/TVF/TVA/PAN Depth) all matched the on-device 'LFO 2' display exactly. The UI's 'LFO 1' tab (different Waveform/Rate/Depth values) has NOT been located yet -- reading the next partial-indexed offset (0x3200, which the doc calls 'Partial LFO 2') returned data IDENTICAL to 0x3000, not a second independent LFO, so 'LFO 1' is not simply 'the next partial's LFO' either. Two live hypotheses, neither confirmed: (a) Easy Mode broadcasts LFO settings to all 4 partials identically (consistent with the same broadcast behavior already seen for TVF Cutoff Frequency), meaning 0x3200 really is partial 2's LFO and coincidentally mirrors partial 1's; or (b) 'LFO 1' lives in a completely different, not-yet-explored block (the doc's separate Tone Synth Common/PMT/Partial hierarchy at relative offsets 0x3C00+ is an unexplored candidate, possibly an analog-modeled second oscillator/LFO layer given the tone under test, 'Ax Piano', appears to be one of Jupiter-X's analog Model Expansion tone types). Also: only the first LFO's non-step-sequencer fields (0x00-0x1D) are mapped below; a large STEP-waveform table (Phase Position, Step 1-16, Step Curve 1-16, offsets ~0x1E-0x44) exists in the official doc past this but wasn't transcribed (only relevant when Waveform=STEP).
